A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoAds benchmark, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. V1 includes supplementary sections I–VI; v2 ends after the references. The supplement's omission is observable in the supplied documents, rather than an extraction failure.

before.justification: V1 reports original model and human evaluations, transcript and CoT experiments, and supplementary complexity sensitivity and prediction analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds evaluations of LLaVA-OneVision, MiniCPM-V2-6, and Gemini-2.5 Pro.

M1.justification: The dataset construction pipeline and DINO-v2-based complexity calculation remain unchanged. Section 5.2 expands the description of guided CoT using intermediate questions and answers; it does not establish a changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 200 advertisement videos and 1,100 questions across visual finding, summary, and reasoning, with unchanged category counts. The dataset complexity comparisons retain their coverage; added models and omitted case illustrations do not establish different datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds LLaVA-OneVision, MiniCPM-V2-6, and Gemini-2.5 Pro, substantially extending the evaluated model set while retaining previous video models. The supplementary CLIP-versus-DINO comparison also disappears. The text-only baseline's relabeling does not establish a model replacement because v1 already inconsistently identified it as GPT-4o in Section 4.2.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds evaluation configurations for LLaVA-OneVision at 7B/32 frames and MiniCPM-V2-6 at 7B/64 frames; Gemini-2.5 Pro's frame budget is unspecified. Existing multiple-choice evaluation and retained model configurations remain unchanged. Newly disclosed human participant and prompting details do not establish reruns or revised sampling.

E4.justification: V2 omits the supplementary neighborhood-size sensitivity analysis in Table 5, prediction case studies in Figures 6–12, and CLIP-versus-DINO examples in Figure 13. This removes substantial robustness and diagnostic evidence. The main frame-count, transcript, and CoT analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for the evaluations. The visual-feature variance used by the complexity metric is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds overall accuracies of 55.08% for LLaVA-OneVision, 57.17% for MiniCPM-V2-6, and 80.04% for Gemini-2.5 Pro, making Gemini the reported leader over the retained Qwen2.5-VL result of 73.35%. These are newly evaluated models, not same-model performance improvements. Existing main-table scores and Figure 4 results are unchanged, while supplementary sensitivity values, duration statistics, and case outcomes disappear.

T1.justification: Section 3.4.1 retains the same exponentially weighted cosine-similarity definition of complexity duration and the normalization Vcpx = 100Dcpx/n. Equation numbering changes, but no mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract adds Gemini-2.5 Pro as the leading model at 80.04%, while retaining the narrower claim that Qwen2.5-VL beats GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 Pro. The introduction explicitly positions VideoAds as complementary to larger benchmarks. The benchmark, complexity-metric, and human-performance-gap contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains that the metric emphasizes coarse visual transitions rather than subtle temporal changes, extending v1's supplementary caveat about visual complexity versus question difficulty. It also explains the need for guided CoT. Conversely, the supplementary interpretations of commonsense-driven failures and CLIP's semantic noise are omitted.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies two human evaluators, gives an example text-only prompt, and clarifies how intermediate CoT answers supply context. It omits v1's 100-question CoT subset size, uniform frame-sampling description, and supplementary filtering details, including the 30-second cutoff and manual versus automatic filtering roles. These are documentation changes; changed underlying samples are not established.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Gemini 2.5, LLaVA-OneVision, and MiniCPM-V, while the GPT-4 technical report and LLaMA-Adapter V2 references disappear. Supplementary Section VI's benchmark survey is omitted, but much of its context remains in the main text. Positioning is refined toward complementing Video-MME and benchmarks of finer temporal changes.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain intact. V2 shortens the title and Section 2, revises the author line, edits language, and rewrites localized positioning and experimental-description passages. The supplementary sections are omitted, but the retained narrative is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The entire supplementary display set—Table 5 and Figures 5–13—is omitted. Table 3 gains model rows and an updated caption, the title block is compacted, and several main figures and tables are resized or repositioned. Figure 4 is relocated without changing its plotted results.

improvement.justification: The added model comparisons and clearer prompting and metric explanations are useful, but v2 loses sensitivity validation, feature-extractor comparisons, case evidence, and reproducibility details while retaining references to the absent appendix. Section 4.2 also still calls Qwen2.5-VL the best-performing model despite Gemini-2.5 Pro's higher Table 3 scores. These losses in completeness and consistency outweigh the limited additions, although the core benchmark remains intact.
